title: Vannevar Bush's Memex and the Dream of Associative Retrieval (1945)
explainer: In his 1945 essay 'As We May Think,' engineer Vannevar Bush imagined the 'memex,' a desk-sized machine that would store a person's books and records and let them follow associative trails between related pieces of information on demand, rather than hunting through a fixed index. RAG systems are a direct descendant of that vision: instead of a model trying to hold everything in its own memory, it reaches out to an external store and pulls back just the pieces relevant to the question at hand.

title: Gerard Salton and the Vector Space Model (1975)
explainer: Working on the SMART retrieval system at Harvard and Cornell through the 1960s, Gerard Salton helped develop the idea — formalized in a 1975 paper with A. Wong and C.S. Yang — of representing documents and search queries as vectors and ranking results by geometric similarity, such as the cosine of the angle between them. Modern RAG retrieval does the same thing with dense neural embeddings instead of word-frequency counts, but the underlying move — turn meaning into a point in space, compare by distance — is Salton's.
